If P lies before Q, angle APB is the exterior angle of PBQ and exceeds the right angle at Q;if P is beyond Q, triangle PQB has its right angle at Q and angle APB is acute. This proves the same inside-circle criterion without dot products. The pentagon is the rectangle 0<=x<=2 pi+1, 0<=y<=4 cut by x+2 y>=4. The diameter AB lies on the cut line, and the circle is centered on that line, so the favorable part is its upper/right semicircle. This semicircle really fits: if x<=0 and x+2 y>=4, then y>=2-x/2 and squared center distance is at least(x-2)^2+(1-x/2)^2=5-5 x+5 x^2/4>=5;similarly y<=0 would give x>=4-2 y and squared distance at least 5(1-y)^2>=5. Its remaining extents satisfy y<=1+sqrt(5)<4 and x<=2+sqrt(5)<5<2 pi+1. Hence no additional clipping occurs. Favorable area is 5 pi/2. The pentagon area is 4*(2 pi+1)-(1/2)*4*2=8 pi, so the ratio is 5/16. Boundaries have area zero.
